name: Alabama AGELINE (Aging and Disability Resource Centers)
description: A statewide line that connects you to the Area Agency on Aging and Aging and Disability Resource Center for your county: meals, in-home services, transportation, caregiver support and senior legal assistance. Military service is not required.
next_step: Call 800-243-5463 (1-800-AGE-LINE) from anywhere in Alabama. Choose a county above for the direct number of its Area Agency on Aging.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.

source_evidence.title: Alabama Department of Senior Services: Area Agencies on Aging are Aging and Disability Resource Centers
source_evidence.scope: Statewide 1-800-AGELINE number and that all 13 agencies are certified ADRCs covering all 67 counties; search excerpt.

name: Medicare counseling (SHIP) for Alabama
organization: Alabama State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP), Department of Senior Services
description: Free, unbiased Medicare counseling from the State Health Insurance Assistance Program. Counselors do not sell insurance.
next_step: Call 800-243-5463 and ask for Medicare counseling, or ask your Area Agency on Aging for the local SHIP counselor.

source_evidence.title: Alabama Department of Senior Services: SHIP
source_evidence.scope: SHIP phone numbers, who it helps and how to reach a local counselor; read in full.

name: Alabama Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program
organization: Alabama Office of the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman, Department of Senior Services
description: Statewide advocacy for residents of nursing homes, assisted living and other long-term care facilities, delivered through 13 regional ombudsman programs.
next_step: Choose your county for its regional ombudsman, or call the state ombudsman office at 334-242-5753. To report suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation of an adult, call the Adult Abuse Hotline at 800-458-7214. For immediate danger, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing or enforcement agency.

source_evidence.title: Alabama Department of Senior Services: Office of the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program
source_evidence.scope: State ombudsman office phone and address; the page lists no regional ombudsmen; read in full.

source_evidence.title: Alabama Department of Human Resources: Adult Protective Services
source_evidence.scope: Adult Abuse Hotline 1-800-458-7214 for reporting suspected mistreatment of adults; search excerpt.

name: Legal Services Alabama
description: Free civil legal help for people with low income and for adults 60 and older. A VA-funded program helps veterans who are homeless or at risk of homelessness. Not criminal defense.
next_step: Call the intake line (English 866-456-4995; Spanish 888-835-3505) or apply at legalservicesalabama.org. Have your county and the legal problem ready, and say if you are a veteran.
constraints: Applicants are screened; income, case type and capacity limits apply. The veterans program serves veterans who are homeless or at risk of homelessness. Phone lines are open Monday–Friday, 8:30 a.m.–4:30 p.m.

source_evidence.title: Legal Services Alabama: veterans services
source_evidence.scope: Intake phones, hours and the veterans program’s eligibility; read in full.

source_evidence.title: Legal Services Alabama: older adults
source_evidence.scope: People 60 and older may qualify for free legal help; search excerpt.

name: VA medical centers serving Alabama
description: Birmingham VA Health Care System: Birmingham VA Medical Center (205-933-8101). Central Alabama Veterans Health Care System: Montgomery campus (334-272-4670) and Tuskegee campus (334-727-0550). Tuscaloosa VA Medical Center (205-554-2000). Community clinics are listed in VA’s facility locator.
next_step: Use VA’s facility locator with your ZIP code to find the closest clinic and its medical center. Not enrolled yet? Ask your Veterans Service Officer for help applying.
constraints: VA does not publish county lists for these systems in the pages read, so this card does not assign counties. Your VA care team may be at a different clinic or system; follow what VA tells you.

name: Housing First, Inc.: veteran housing help (SSVF)
description: VA-funded Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF, grant 12-AL-002): case management, help keeping a home, rapid rehousing and short-term financial help for low-income veteran households.
next_step: Call SSVF intake with your county and housing situation: whether you are homeless now or at risk of losing housing, and who lives with you. A second intake number is listed: 251-303-8058.
constraints: Serves only the areas listed; check that yours is included. Veteran-household, income and housing-status screening applies.
County and intake details come from VA’s FY26 SSVF provider intake list; confirm current service when calling.
